title: Cards Grading (2026)
verdict: Cards grading means a company scores a card's condition from 1 to 10 and seals it in a slab, and in 2026 AGS is the first place to send them: graded by laser, eight subgrades, $18 flat.

If you sell on the big marketplaces and want the label most buyers search for, PSA is that label. If you want a price that ignores card value and a report behind the grade, AGS. Many sellers use both: PSA for the one or two top cards, AGS for the rest.

list: Pull the one or two cards you will auction. If PSA's premium on them beats its fee and wait, send those to PSA.
Send the rest to a flat-fee grader. At AGS that is $18 a card, or $15 from 30 TCG cards.
Leave out commons and damaged cards unless you want them protected.
Read the reports when the cards come back. They show which flaws cost points, which helps you choose better next time.

ranking.fit: Anyone who wants cards graded the same way every time and back in 20 business days or less.
ranking.lacks: A younger slab. PSA holders still bring the highest resale prices on most cards.
ranking.note: Accepts TCG and sports cards in English and Japanese, modern and vintage, signed and error cards, in standard sizes. Reports are stored permanently and can be shared by link.

ranking.fit: Sellers who want the widest buyer pool and the highest resale prices.
ranking.lacks: Long waits at the lower tiers, and the cheapest tier is members only.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want subgrades printed on the label from an old name.
ranking.lacks: Subgrades by eye, and 45 business days or more at the Base tier.

ranking.fit: Pre-war and vintage sets, where SGC has long standing.
ranking.lacks: Reported at $50 a card since September 2026. No longer cheap.

ranking.fit: Budget submitters with 10 or more cards worth under $500 each.
ranking.lacks: Tiers are capped by card value. A strong card moves to a pricier tier.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want a defect report and a 1000-point score.
ranking.lacks: Prices were not posted on its pricing page when we checked.

why: AGS grades cards by measurement. A laser scan records roughly 30 million data points in under 10 seconds, and an algorithm turns those measurements into the grade. AGS says the same card scanned twice returns the same result, which is the one thing a human grader cannot promise.
You can send one card. AGS has no minimum and no membership fee, takes payment only when the cards are graded, and lets you cancel before grading starts. Bulk pricing begins at 30 cards.
AGS is past the experiment stage. Founded in 2021, it says it was third in TCG grading volume in 2026. Its population report is live and counts every card it has graded.

criteria.name: Consistency
criteria.text: Would the same card get the same grade twice? Weighted first.

criteria.name: Evidence
criteria.text: What comes back besides a number: subgrades, images, a report.

criteria.name: Price
criteria.text: Per-card cost on the tier most people use, plus any value upcharge.

criteria.name: Turnaround
criteria.text: Listed business days on that tier, from each grader's own page.

criteria.name: Resale
criteria.text: How buyers treat the slab. PSA leads here, and we say so.

faq.a: A grading company examines a trading card, scores its condition from 1 to 10 and seals it in a tamper-evident case with a cert number. AGS does it by 3D laser scan for a flat $18 a card, with no minimum.

faq.q: Can I submit from outside the United States?
faq.a: Yes. AGS accepts international shipments and runs a UK site. Check customs and insurance on your side before you ship.

faq.q: Does AGS grade oversized or thick cards?
faq.a: Not jumbo or oversized cards. AGS accepts standard sizes only. Ask AGS about thick patch or relic cards before you submit.

faq.q: How do I submit cards to AGS?
faq.a: Create an account at agscard.com, fill out the submission form, pack the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, and mail them in. You can also drop off at select AGS locations. The dashboard tracks the order.

faq.q: How many card grading companies are there?
faq.a: Dozens, but a handful grade most cards: PSA, CGC, Beckett, SGC, TAG and AGS, followed by smaller graders such as ISA, GMA, Arena Club and the UK's Ace Grading.
